answer: Along the towpath the surveyor measures every milepost, and the survey seals the distance between the locks for the whole canal. A canyon mile claimed as walked fails the survey: the post must have stood at the ivory of the towpath, and a mile never walked has no post to show. Faking a canal means hiring a surveyor, forging forty post readings and paying 11,200, and the forge survey is checked before every toll is set, so a mile whose post was never measured is walked again from scratch.
